Chafa
=====

Chafa is a command-line utility that converts image data, including
animated GIFs, into graphics formats or ANSI/Unicode character art suitable
for display in a terminal. It has broad feature support, allowing it to be
used on devices ranging from historical teleprinters to modern terminal
emulators and everything in between.

The core functionality is provided by a C library with a public,
well-documented API.

Both library and frontend tools are covered by the Lesser GPL license,
version 3 or later (LGPLv3+).

For the most up-to-date information, please see https://hpjansson.org/chafa/

Installing with package manager
-------------------------------

Chafa is available as packages for many software distributions. A few are
listed below, along with their command-line installation instructions:

Arch Linux .... pacman -S chafa
Brew .......... brew install chafa
Debian ........ apt install chafa
Fedora ........ dnf install chafa
FreeBSD ....... pkg install chafa
Gentoo ........ emerge media-gfx/chafa
Guix .......... guix install chafa
Kali Linux .... apt install chafa
MacPorts ...... port install chafa
OpenBSD ....... pkg_add chafa
openSUSE ...... zypper in chafa
Ubuntu ........ apt install chafa

On Windows, Chafa can be installed via Scoop and Winget:

Scoop ....... scoop install chafa
Winget ....... winget install hpjansson.Chafa

See https://hpjansson.org/chafa/download/ for more.

Usage
-----

Basic usage:

  chafa [OPTIONS] [IMAGE...]

Common options:

  -s, --size <WxH>        Set output size in character cells
  -c, --colors <mode>     Color mode (2, 16, 240, 256, full, etc.)
  --symbols <symbols>     Select symbol sets for character art output
  --format <format>       Output format (symbols, sixels, kitty, iterm)
  --animate <on|off>      Enable/disable animation
  -d, --duration <secs>   Animation duration
  --bg <color>            Background color
  --fg <color>            Foreground color
  -h, --help              Show help

Examples:

  # Convert an image to terminal art
  chafa image.jpg

  # Set specific output size
  chafa --size 80x25 image.png

  # Animate a GIF
  chafa animation.gif

  # Use Sixel graphics (if terminal supports it)
  chafa --format sixels image.jpg

Language bindings
-----------------

Chafa has bindings for other programming languages:

# Chafa

## About

Chafa is a command-line utility that converts image data, including
animated GIFs, into graphics formats or ANSI/Unicode character art suitable
for display in a terminal. It has broad feature support, allowing it to be
used on devices ranging from historical teleprinters to modern terminal
emulators and everything in between.

The core functionality is provided by a C library with a public,
well-documented API.

Both library and frontend tools are covered by the Lesser GPL license,
version 3 or later (LGPLv3+).

## Features

- Converts images (including animated GIFs) to terminal-displayable formats
- Supports multiple output formats: ANSI/Unicode character art, Sixel graphics, iTerm2 inline images, Kitty graphics protocol
- Works with various terminal types from historical teleprinters to modern emulators
- Handles multiple image formats as input
- Animation support with customizable playback

## Usage

Basic usage:

```sh
chafa [OPTIONS] [IMAGE...]
```

### Common Options

- `-s, --size <WxH>` - Set output size in character cells
- `-c, --colors <mode>` - Color mode (2, 16, 240, 256, full, etc.)
- `--symbols <symbols>` - Select symbol sets for character art output
- `--format <format>` - Output format (symbols, sixels, kitty, iterm)
- `--animate <on|off>` - Enable/disable animation
- `-d, --duration <seconds>` - Animation duration
- `--bg <color>` - Background color
- `--fg <color>` - Foreground color

### Examples

Convert an image to terminal art:
```sh
chafa image.jpg
```

Set specific output size:
```sh
chafa --size 80x25 image.png
```

Animate a GIF with limited duration:
```sh
chafa --duration 10 animation.gif
```

Use Sixel graphics (if terminal supports it):
```sh
chafa --format sixels image.jpg
```

## Package Installation

Chafa is available as packages for many software distributions:

- **Arch Linux**: `pacman -S chafa`
- **Debian/Ubuntu**: `apt install chafa`
- **Fedora**: `dnf install chafa`
- **FreeBSD**: `pkg install chafa`
- **Gentoo**: `emerge media-gfx/chafa`
- **macOS (Brew)**: `brew install chafa`
- **macOS (MacPorts)**: `port install chafa`
- **OpenBSD**: `pkg_add chafa`
- **openSUSE**: `zypper in chafa`
- **Windows (Scoop)**: `scoop install chafa`
- **Windows (Winget)**: `winget install hpjansson.Chafa`

## Links

- Official website: https://hpjansson.org/chafa/
- Gallery: https://hpjansson.org/chafa/gallery/
- API documentation: https://hpjansson.org/chafa/ref/

## Language Bindings

- **Python**: https://chafapy.mage.black/
- **JavaScript/WebAssembly**: https://github.com/hectorm/chafa-wasm

def run(args, env=None, stdin_data=None, timeout=5):
    base=dict(os.environ)
    base.update({"TERM":"xterm","COLUMNS":"80","LINES":"25"})
    if env: base.update(env)
    try:
        p=subprocess.run(["./executable"]+args, input=stdin_data, capture_output=True, env=base, timeout=timeout)
        return p.returncode, p.stdout or b"", p.stderr or b""
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as e:

# Test -- handling, combined short opts, --help/--version precedence, unknown, stdin caching

    (["--symbols"], None),
    (["--bg"], None),
    (["--files"], None),  # missing arg? but earlier it treated file content?
    (["--files="], None),
    (["--files=/nonexistent"], None),
    (["--files0=/nonexistent"], None),
    (["--glyph-file"], None),
    (["--threads"], None),
    (["--work"], None),
    (["--optimize"], None),
    (["--duration"], None),
    (["--speed"], None),
]
for args, stdin_data in tests:
    rc,out,err=run(args, stdin_data=stdin_data)
    print(f"{args} => rc={rc} err={err[:400]!r} out_len={len(out)} out={out[:200]!r}")

import subprocess, os
def run(args, env=None, stdin_data=None, timeout=5):
    base=dict(os.environ)
    base.update({"TERM":"xterm","COLUMNS":"80","LINES":"25"})
    if env: base.update(env)
    try:
        p=subprocess.run(["./executable"]+args, input=stdin_data, capture_output=True, env=base, timeout=timeout)
        return p.returncode, p.stdout or b"", p.stderr or b""
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as e:
        return "TIMEOUT", e.stdout or b"", e.stderr or b""

# More framing: grid, multiple files, view-size, margins, etc.
def show(args, env=None):
    rc,out,err=run(args, env=env)
    print(f"ARGS {args} env={env} rc={rc} err={err[:200]!r}")
    # show escaped
    print(f"  out_len={len(out)} out={out[:600]!r}")
    print()

show(["-g", "assets/pixel.png", "assets/pixel.jpeg"])
show(["--grid=2x2", "assets/pixel.png", "assets/pixel.jpeg"])
show(["--size=20x10", "assets/pixel.png", "assets/pixel.jpeg"])
show(["--view-size=40x10", "assets/pixel.png"])
show(["--margin-bottom=5", "--view-size=40x10", "assets/pixel.png"])
# COLUMNS/LINES env effect
show(["assets/pixel.png"], env={"COLUMNS":"40","LINES":"10"})
show(["assets/taxic.jpg"], env={"COLUMNS":"40","LINES":"10"})
show(["--size=80x25", "assets/taxic.jpg"])
show(["-c", "none", "--size=80x25", "assets/taxic.jpg"])
PY"}

import subprocess, os
def run(args, env=None, stdin_data=None, timeout=5):
    base=dict(os.environ)
    base.update({"TERM":"xterm","COLUMNS":"80","LINES":"25"})
    if env: base.update(env)
    try:
        p=subprocess.run(["./executable"]+args, input=stdin_data, capture_output=True, env=base, timeout=timeout)
        return p.returncode, p.stdout or b"", p.stderr or b""
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as e:
        return "TIMEOUT", e.stdout or b"", e.stderr or b""

# symbols tests
for s in ["ascii","block","braille","none","all","space","solid","wide","narrow"]:
    rc,out,err=run(["--symbols="+s,"--size=5x3","-c","none","assets/taxic.jpg"])
    print(f"s={s} rc={rc} len={len(out)} out={out[:300]!r} err={err[:100]!r}")

# fill
for f in ["block","none"]:
    rc,out,err=run(["--fill="+f,"--size=5x3","-c","none","assets/taxic.jpg"])
    print(f"fill={f} rc={rc} len={len(out)} out={out[:300]!r}")

# fg-only, invert
for args in [
    ["--fg-only","--size=5x3","assets/taxic.jpg"],
    ["--invert","--size=5x3","assets/taxic.jpg"],
    ["--bg=red","--fg=blue","--size=5x3","assets/taxic.jpg"],
    ["--threshold=0.5","--size=5x3","assets/card-32c-alpha.png"],
    ["--threshold=0.0","--size=5x3","assets/card-32c-alpha.png"],
    ["--dither=ordered","-c","16","--size=5x3","assets/taxic.jpg"],
    ["--dither=none","-c","16","--size=5x3","assets/taxic.jpg"],
]:
    rc,out,err=run(args)
    print(f"{args} rc={rc} len={len(out)} out={out[:400]!r} err={err[:100]!r}")
PY"}

import subprocess, os
def run(args, env=None, stdin_data=None, timeout=5):
    base=dict(os.environ)
    base.update({"TERM":"xterm","COLUMNS":"80","LINES":"25"})
    if env: base.update(env)
    try:
        p=subprocess.run(["./executable"]+args, input=stdin_data, capture_output=True, env=base, timeout=timeout)
        return p.returncode, p.stdout or b"", p.stderr or b""
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as e:
        return "TIMEOUT", e.stdout or b"", e.stderr or b""

# Test all image formats quickly with -c none --size small to see decoding works
for f in ["assets/pixel.png","assets/pixel.jpeg","assets/pixel.qoi","assets/pixel.tiff","assets/pixel.webp","assets/pixel.xwd","assets/noise-32x32.png","assets/noise-32x32-indexed.png","assets/card-32c-alpha.png","assets/card-full-alpha.png","assets/taxic.jpg"]:
    rc,out,err=run(["-c","none","--size=10x5",f])
    print(f"{f} rc={rc} len={len(out)} err={err[:100]!r} out={out[:80]!r}")

# Test anim gifs with animate off
for f in ["assets/anim.gif","assets/anim-local-cmaps.gif"]:
    rc,out,err=run(["-c","none","--size=10x5","--animate=off",f])
    print(f"{f} animate off rc={rc} len={len(out)} err={err[:100]!r} out={out[:120]!r}")
    # also try with animate on but duration 0? Should still render single frame quickly
    rc,out,err=run(["-c","none","--size=10x5","--animate=on","--duration=0",f], timeout=5)
    print(f"  animate on duration0 rc={rc} len={len(out)}")

# SVG? No svg asset. Create simple svg?
open("/tmp/test.svg","w").write('<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="10" height="10"><rect width="10" height="10" fill="red"/></svg>')
rc,out,err=run(["-c","none","--size=10x5","/tmp/test.svg"])
print(f"svg rc={rc} len={len(out)} err={err[:200]!r} out={out[:200]!r}")
PY"}

import subprocess, os, re
def run(args, env=None, stdin_data=None, timeout=5):
    base=dict(os.environ)
    base.update({"TERM":"xterm","COLUMNS":"80","LINES":"25"})
    if env: base.update(env)
    p=subprocess.run(["./executable"]+args, input=stdin_data, capture_output=True, env=base, timeout=timeout)
    return p.returncode, p.stdout or b"", p.stderr or b""

def strip_ansi(data: bytes):
    # remove ESC sequences: ESC[ ... letter, ESCP ... ESC\, ESC] ... BEL or ESC\, etc.
    # Simplified: remove \x1b\[.*?[@-~], \x1bP.*?\x1b\\, \x1b].*?(?:\x07|\x1b\\), \x1b[?25l/h, etc.
    import re
    s = data.decode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    # Remove OSC hyperlink etc: ESC ] 8 ;; ... ESC \
    s = re.sub(r'\x1b\]8;;.*?\x1b\\', '', s)
    s = re.sub(r'\x1b\].*?(?:\x07|\x1b\\)', '', s)
    s = re.sub(r'\x1bP.*?(\x1b\\|\x07)', '', s, flags=re.DOTALL)
    s = re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;?]*[A-Za-z]', '', s)
    s = re.sub(r'\x1b[()][0-9A-B]', '', s)
    s = re.sub(r'\x1b[=>MED78c]', '', s)
    s = re.sub(r'\x1b\ timest', '', s)
    return s

def cell_dims(args):
    rc,out,err=run(args)
    stripped=strip_ansi(out)
    # For symbols, output is lines of chars. Remove hide/show? Already stripped.
    # Split by \n, filter? The framing includes hide/show which are stripped, leaving content lines.
    # For polite off, starts with hide, ends with show, stripped leaves content.
    lines=stripped.split('\n')
    # Remove trailing empty due to final \n? The output ends with \n + show. So last element may be ''?
    # Let's show lines
    print(f"ARGS {args} rc={rc} len={len(out)}")
    print(f"  stripped repr: {stripped[:500]!r}")
    print(f"  lines: {len(lines)} lens: {[len(l) for l in lines[:10]]}")
    # Count non-empty?

import struct, zlib

def png_size(path):
    with open(path,'rb') as f:
        data=f.read(30)
        # PNG signature 8 bytes, then IHDR chunk: length 4, type 4, data 13
        if data[:8]!=b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n':
            return None
        w=struct.unpack('>I', data[16:20])[0]
        h=struct.unpack('>I', data[20:24])[0]
        return w,h

def jpeg_size(path):
    with open(path,'rb') as f:
        d=f.read()
    # scan markers
    i=2
    if d[0:2]!=b'\xff\xd8':
        return None
    while i < len(d):
        if d[i]!=0xFF:
            i+=1
            continue
        marker=d[i+1]
        if marker in (0xD8,0xD9):
            i+=2
            continue
        if 0xD0 <= marker <= 0xD7:
            i+=2
            continue
        if marker==0x01:
            i+=2
            continue
        length=struct.unpack('>H', d[i+2:i+4])[0]
        if marker in (0xC0,0xC1,0xC2,0xC3):
            h=struct.unpack('>H', d[i+5:i+7])[0]
            w=struct.unpack('>H', d[i+7:i+9])[0]
            return w,h
        i+=2+length
    return None

def gif_size(path):
    with open(path,'rb') as f:
        d=f.read(10)
        if d[:6] not in (b'GIF87a',b'GIF89a'):
            return None
        w=struct.unpack('<H', d[6:8])[0]
        h=struct.unpack('<H', d[8:10])[0]
        return w,h

def qoi_size(path):
    with open(path,'rb') as f:
        d=f.read(14)
        if d[:4]!=b'qoif':
            return None
        w=struct.unpack('>I', d[4:8])[0]
        h=struct.unpack('>I', d[8:12])[0]
        return w,h

def webp_size(path):
    with open(path,'rb') as f:
        d=f.read(30)
        # RIFF....WEBP
        if d[:4]!=b'RIFF' or d[8:12]!=b'WEBP':
            return None
        chunk=d[12:16]
        print(path, chunk, d[12:30].hex())
        if chunk==b'VP8 ':
            # frame header? w/h at bytes?
            # VP8 frame: 3 bytes frame tag, 3 bytes start code, 2 bytes w, 2 bytes h
            w=struct.unpack('<H', d[26:28])[0] & 0x3FFF
            h=struct.unpack('<H', d[28:30])[0] & 0x3FFF
            return w,h
        elif chunk==b'VP8L':
            # lossless: 1 byte signature 0x2f, 14 bits w-1, 14 bits h-1?
            # bytes after chunk size?
            # VP8L header: 4 bytes chunk size, 1 byte signature, 4 bytes w/h?
            # Let's parse: d[16:20] size, d[20]=0x2f, d[21:25] contains dims
            b1,b2,b3,b4=d[21],d[22],d[23],d[24]
            w=((b2 & 0x3F)<<8 | b1)+1
            h=((b4 & 0xF)<<10 | (b3<<2) | ((b2 & 0xC0)>>6))+1
            return w,h
        elif chunk==b'VP8X':
            w= int.from_bytes(d[24:27],'little')+1
            h= int.from_bytes(d[27:30],'little')+1
            return w,h
        return None

def tiff_size(path):
    with open(path,'rb') as f:
        d=f.read(200)
        endian=d[:2]
        if endian==b'II':
            fmt='<H'
            fmtL='<L'
        elif endian==b'MM':
            fmt='>H'
            fmtL='>L'
        else:
            return None
        # offset to IFD
        off=struct.unpack(fmtL, d[4:8])[0]
        # Need to read at off
        with open(path,'rb') as f2:
            f2.seek(off)
            n=struct.unpack(fmt, f2.read(2))[0]
            w=h=None
            for _ in range(n):
                entry=f2.read(12)
                tag=struct.unpack(fmt, entry[0:2])[0]
                typ=struct.unpack(fmt, entry[2:4])[0]
                cnt=struct.unpack(fmtL, entry[4:8])[0]
                val=entry[8:12]
                if tag==256:
                    if typ==3:
                        w=struct.unpack(fmt, val[0:2])[0]
                    elif typ==4:
                        w=struct.unpack(fmtL, val[0:4])[0]
                elif tag==257:
                    if typ==3:
                        h=struct.unpack(fmt, val[0:2])[0]
                    elif typ==4:
                        h=struct.unpack(fmtL, val[0:4])[0]
            return w,h

def xwd_size(path):
    with open(path,'rb') as f:
        d=f.read(200)
        # XWD header: big endian? struct?
        # header_size(4), file_version(4), pixmap_format(4), pixmap_depth(4), pixmap_width(4), pixmap_height(4), ...
        # All big endian?
        vals=struct.unpack('>7I', d[:28])
        print(path, vals)
        return vals[4], vals[5]

for p in ["assets/pixel.png","assets/pixel.jpeg","assets/anim.gif","assets/pixel.qoi","assets/pixel.webp","assets/pixel.tiff","assets/pixel.xwd","assets/taxic.jpg","assets/noise-32x32.png"]:
    print(p, "png", png_size(p) if p.endswith(".png") else "", "jpeg", jpeg_size(p) if p.endswith(".jpg") or p.endswith(".jpeg") else "", "gif", gif_size(p) if p.endswith(".gif") else "", "qoi", qoi_size(p) if p.endswith(".qoi") else "", "webp", webp_size(p) if p.endswith(".webp") else "", "tiff", tiff_size(p) if p.endswith(".tiff") else "", "xwd", xwd_size(p) if p.endswith(".xwd") else "")

# Also check via libgd for comparison

import struct, zlib

def png_size(path):
    with open(path,'rb') as f:
        data=f.read(30)
        # PNG signature 8 bytes, then IHDR chunk: length 4, type 4, data 13
        if data[:8]!=b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n':
            return None
        w=struct.unpack('>I', data[16:20])[0]
        h=struct.unpack('>I', data[20:24])[0]
        return w,h

def jpeg_size(path):
    with open(path,'rb') as f:
        d=f.read()
    # scan markers
    i=2
    if d[0:2]!=b'\xff\xd8':
        return None
    while i < len(d):
        if d[i]!=0xFF:
            i+=1
            continue
        marker=d[i+1]
        if marker in (0xD8,0xD9):
            i+=2
            continue
        if 0xD0 <= marker <= 0xD7:
            i+=2
            continue
        if marker==0x01:
            i+=2
            continue
        length=struct.unpack('>H', d[i+2:i+4])[0]
        if marker in (0xC0,0xC1,0xC2,0xC3):
            h=struct.unpack('>H', d[i+5:i+7])[0]
            w=struct.unpack('>H', d[i+7:i+9])[0]
            return w,h
        i+=2+length
    return None

def gif_size(path):
    with open(path,'rb') as f:
        d=f.read(10)
        if d[:6] not in (b'GIF87a',b'GIF89a'):
            return None
        w=struct.unpack('<H', d[6:8])[0]
        h=struct.unpack('<H', d[8:10])[0]
        return w,h

def qoi_size(path):
    with open(path,'rb') as f:
        d=f.read(14)
        if d[:4]!=b'qoif':
            return None
        w=struct.unpack('>I', d[4:8])[0]
        h=struct.unpack('>I', d[8:12])[0]
        return w,h

def webp_size(path):
    with open(path,'rb') as f:
        d=f.read(30)
        # RIFF....WEBP
        if d[:4]!=b'RIFF' or d[8:12]!=b'WEBP':
            return None
        chunk=d[12:16]
        print(path, chunk, d[12:30].hex())
        if chunk==b'VP8 ':
            # frame header? w/h at bytes?
            # VP8 frame: 3 bytes frame tag, 3 bytes start code, 2 bytes w, 2 bytes h
            w=struct.unpack('<H', d[26:28])[0] & 0x3FFF
            h=struct.unpack('<H', d[28:30])[0] & 0x3FFF
            return w,h
        elif chunk==b'VP8L':
            # lossless: 1 byte signature 0x2f, 14 bits w-1, 14 bits h-1?
            # bytes after chunk size?
            # VP8L header: 4 bytes chunk size, 1 byte signature, 4 bytes w/h?
            # Let's parse: d[16:20] size, d[20]=0x2f, d[21:25] contains dims
            b1,b2,b3,b4=d[21],d[22],d[23],d[24]

Chafa
=====

Chafa is a command-line utility that converts image data, including
animated GIFs, into graphics formats or ANSI/Unicode character art suitable
for display in a terminal. It has broad feature support, allowing it to be
used on devices ranging from historical teleprinters to modern terminal
emulators and everything in between.

The core functionality is provided by a C library with a public,
well-documented API.

Both library and frontend tools are covered by the Lesser GPL license,
version 3 or later (LGPLv3+).

For the most up-to-date information, please see https://hpjansson.org/chafa/

Installing with package manager
-------------------------------

Chafa is available as packages for many software distributions. A few are
listed below, along with their command-line installation instructions:

Arch Linux .... pacman -S chafa
Brew .......... brew install chafa
Debian ........ apt install chafa
Fedora ........ dnf install chafa
FreeBSD ....... pkg install chafa
Gentoo ........ emerge media-gfx/chafa
Guix .......... guix install chafa
Kali Linux .... apt install chafa
MacPorts ...... port install chafa
OpenBSD ....... pkg_add chafa
openSUSE ...... zypper in chafa
Ubuntu ........ apt install chafa

On Windows, Chafa can be installed via Scoop and Winget:

Scoop ....... scoop install chafa
Winget ....... winget install hpjansson.Chafa

See https://hpjansson.org/chafa/download/ for more.

Usage
-----

Basic usage:

  chafa [OPTIONS] [IMAGE...]

    import re

    s=re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;?]*[A-Za-z]', '', s)

    e1=(p1.stderr or b"").replace(b"./executable",b"P")

    ok_rc=(p1.returncode==p2.returncode)
    ok_err=(e1==e2)
    # For stdout, check dims for symbols, markers for pixel
    def strip(d):
        s=d.decode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
        s=re.sub(r'\x1b\]8;;.*?\x1b\\', '', s)
        s=re.sub(r'\x1b\].*?(?:\x07|\x1b\\)', '', s)
        s=re.sub(r'\x1bP.*?(\x1b\\|\x07)', '', s, flags=re.DOTALL)
        s=re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;?]*[A-Za-z]', '', s)
        s=re.sub(r'\x1b[()][0-9A-B]', '', s)
        s=re.sub(r'\x1b[=>MED78c]', '', s)
        return s
    s1=strip(p1.stdout or b""); s2=strip(p2.stdout or b"")
    l1=s1.split('\n'); l2=s2.split('\n')
    if l1 and l1[-1]=='': l1=l1[:-1]
    if l2 and l2[-1]=='': l2=l2[:-1]
    w1=len(l1[0]) if l1 else 0; h1=len(l1); w2=len(l2[0]) if l2 else 0; h2=len(l2)
    is_pixel = any("sixels" in a or "kitty" in a or "iterm" in a for a in args)
    if is_pixel:
        m1=(b"\x1bP" in (p1.stdout or b"") or b"\x1b_G" in (p1.stdout or b"") or b"1337" in (p1.stdout or b""))
        m2=(b"\x1bP" in (p2.stdout or b"") or b"\x1b_G" in (p2.stdout or b"") or b"1337" in (p2.stdout or b""))
        ok_dim=(m1==m2)
    else:
        ok_dim=(w1==w2 and h1==h2)
    ok=ok_rc and ok_err and ok_dim
    print(f"{args} {'OK' if ok else 'FAIL'} rc{p1.returncode}/{p2.returncode} err{'OK' if ok_err else 'DIFF'} dims{w1}x{h1}/{w2}x{h2} {'DIMOK' if ok_dim else 'DIMDIFF'}")
    if not ok:
        print(f"  err1={e1[:150]!r}")
        print(f"  err2={e2[:150]!r}")
    return ok
